name: Orange brown
lede: Orange brown is a plain description for a mid-dark brown that leans toward orange, the hue of burnt iron earths, dead bracken and the tawny of a dry leaf.

sections.title: A description, not a coinage
sections.body: Orange brown is two color words joined, and the books use it as a gloss rather than a title [1]. Paterson defines bracken as the olive-brown or orange brown of the dead fern [2]. St Clair's glossary of color words defines tawny as tan-colored, orange-brown [3]. Werner's old nomenclature, as Baty prints it, describes a deep orange-coloured brown as chestnut brown tinged with reddish brown and a touch of orange brown [4]. The swatch sits close to [[sienna]], [[brown]] and [[orange]] in the data [5].

sections.title: Iron and madder
sections.body: The pigments that give this color are mostly iron. Martel wrote in 1860 that heating Mars yellow, a manufactured iron oxide, gives orange, brown, red and violet Mars pigments depending on the heat [6]. Salter in 1869 described Cory's yellow madder as an orange-brown of burnt sienna hue, prepared from [[irresistible]] [7]. Among minerals, pararealgar, the arsenic sulfide that realgar becomes in light, ranges from yellow through orange-yellow to orange-brown [8].

sections.title: In painting
sections.body: Ball finds a deep orange-brown in Rembrandt's *Portrait of Jacob Trip*, painted about 1661, mixed from red and yellow lake with smalt [9].

sections.title: In color systems
sections.body: The color appears in several systems. RAL lists it as 8023, ISCC-NBS 1955 files it under block 16, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary has a nearby plate named Spice, first recorded in 1922 [5]. The Japanese color biwacha, loquat-tree brown, and chōjizome, clove-dyed, are close matches [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Orange brown is common in painting as photographed: 589 of the 23,531 paintings in the ColorHub archive carry a color this close, 2.48 percent [10]. Its nearest named color is Sienna, at a color distance (ΔE) of 4.9 [5].
